confirmed: Read the entire local markdown through the references and checked the relevant PDF pages and extracted Tables 1-3. The source is the 18-page arXiv:2411.08588v1 [cs.HC] preprint dated 13 Nov 2024; the title and authors match the form (PDF p. 1, title block and arXiv stamp; pp. 17-18, final references).
The formative study involved six fashion professionals interviewed about their design process and AI use; it did not assign AI assistance or score creative output (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.1-3.2).

The evaluation analyzed 10 people, each using both CLAY and the DALL-E baseline; the two arm counts refer to the same people and must not be added. Ten is below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 2, Introduction; p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2; p. 16, Conclusion).

The paper reports 12 recruited, final demographics of three males and seven females, and exclusion of two participants who used previous designs. The form correctly preserves the awkward recruitment wording and leaves randomized counts null (PDF p. 8, Section 5; p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2).

The evaluation participants were current fashion professionals with 2 to 5 years of experience, invited to a university laboratory and compensated $50; they were distinct from the formative sample (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 5.1).

CLAY uses GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT) and DALL-E; the baseline uses the same DALL-E API without CLAY keyword extraction, hierarchical recommendations, or combination image generation. This is a comparison of AI configurations (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; p. 9, Section 5.2).

Participants created moodboards and pen-and-paper design sketches in both conditions. Tool order was counterbalanced, while style keywords were randomly provided; random assignment of AI condition order is not stated (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2).
All three reported strings match the PDF: CSI total score, CLAY mean 84.6, std 13.47; baseline mean 62.9, std 22.70; P = 0.018, * (PDF p. 11, Table 3, Score row).
Interaction Count: CLAY mean 6.6, std 2.17; baseline mean 11.4, std 6.87; p = 0.049, * (PDF p. 10, Table 1, Interaction Count row).
NASA-TLX total score: CLAY mean 29.0, std 15.87; baseline mean 46.6, std 19.59; P = 0.04, * (PDF p. 11, Table 2, Score row).

The one-line finding correctly reports the 10-person sample, CSI means 84.6 versus 62.9 with p = 0.018, and interaction means 6.6 versus 11.4 with p = 0.049 (PDF p. 2, Introduction; p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Table 3).

CSI and NASA-TLX are post-task survey measures; interaction count measures the process. No creativity or diversity score on the produced moodboards or designs is reported; qualitative examples do not supply such scores. Core = no and context_class = none are supported (PDF p. 9, Sections 5.3-5.4; pp. 10-11, Tables 1-3; pp. 10-14, Section 6.2 and Figures 9-11).

This is an original system-development and user-evaluation paper, not a synthesis; the synthesis counts remain null and no pooled estimates apply (PDF p. 4, Section 3; pp. 8-14, Sections 5-6). No appendix or supplementary material is identified in the document (complete markdown; PDF ends with references on pp. 17-18).
summary: The reported statistics and 10-person evaluation sample match the PDF, and no study reports both randomized AI assistance and creativity or diversity scored on output. Corrections concern the unsupported RCT classification, the omitted formative-study entry, and the conflicting interview durations.
